ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Rachel Carson

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for sinus symptoms on ribociclib

text.paragraph: Blocked nose, facial pressure, and cough for five days. [S]

Ms. Carson is a 53-year-old woman with stage IIB hormone receptor-positive left breast cancer, five weeks into letrozole and on day 8 of her second 28-day cycle of ribociclib. Five days ago she developed a blocked nose, clear then yellow discharge, pressure over both cheeks, a sore throat, and a dry cough. She has had no fever on her home thermometer, checked twice a day as the oncology team taught her, and no chills, breathlessness, or chest pain. The symptoms are no worse than three days ago. She has used saline spray. She called the oncology nurse line, who asked her to be seen today with a blood count. She wanted to know whether this was dangerous on ribociclib and whether she should stop it, and asked for a plain answer. [S]

list.item:
Acute viral rhinosinusitis (J01.90). Five days of symptoms that are not worsening, with no high fever and no worsening after early improvement, fits a viral illness. Colored discharge alone does not mean a bacterial infection, so an antibiotic is not indicated now. [S]
Saline irrigation twice a day and acetaminophen as needed, no more than 3000 mg a day; no ibuprofen or naproxen after her ulcer.
If symptoms last beyond ten days, worsen after improving, or a fever of 39 °C or more develops, an antibiotic will be needed: amoxicillin-clavulanate, which does not prolong the QT interval.
Avoid azithromycin, clarithromycin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin, and over-the-counter cough medicines with the same effect, while on ribociclib.

Neutropenia on ribociclib (C50.412). Absolute neutrophil count 1.2, grade 2, an expected effect of ribociclib, without fever. She was told plainly that this does not make the cold dangerous, and that grade 2 neutropenia does not require stopping or reducing ribociclib. A fever would change that, because infection with a low neutrophil count needs same-day treatment. [S]
Continue ribociclib and letrozole without change, after confirming this with the oncology team by telephone.
Temperature twice a day; a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, chills, or breathlessness means calling the oncology line the same day, at any hour.
Blood count as planned at the start of the next cycle.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer, Version 5.2025 (2025); KISQALI (ribociclib) tablets: prescribing information (dosage for early breast cancer; QT, hepatotoxicity, and neutropenia monitoring) (2026); IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis in Children and Adults. Clin Infect Dis 2012;54(8):e72-e112 (2012)

Follow-up: Telephone check in three days. Return if symptoms pass ten days or worsen. Oncology blood count at the start of the next cycle. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-08: monitoring visit at the start of the fourth ribociclib cycle. [S]
